A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mean-expansion-layer research. Their complete main texts, Figures 1–8, Tables 1–2, and Appendices A–G are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original gridworld, Atari, and LunarLander experiments, including performance, sensitivity, overestimation, and action-gap results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised gridworld and RMSprop comparison curves.

M1.justification: The mean-expansion transformation, default coefficient choices, IB-DQN/IB-IQN construction, and tabular updates remain unchanged. The added JAX implementation expresses the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix F expands the reported RMSprop/Huber comparison from 55 to 57 Atari games, without identifying the two additional games. The main Atari-57 evaluation, gridworld, LunarLander-v3, and Atari-5-Val tuning coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: tabular Q-learning, DQN, Dueling DQN, RDQ, IQN, and the implicit-baseline variants. The RMSprop comparison still evaluates DQN against IB-DQN(n).

E3.justification: Appendix F changes the game pool used for IQM aggregation from 55 to 57 environments. The stated optimizer, loss, training budget, and aggregation metric remain unchanged, as do the main Atari protocol and gridworld sweep. No concrete replacement IQN exploration schedule is specified.

E4.justification: Figures 2 and 6 revise evidence for the existing gridworld coefficient/sample-budget analysis and robustness to RMSprop with Huber loss. The questions tested remain the same; the Atari/LunarLander sensitivity, overestimation, and action-gap analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Seed counts and uncertainty-reporting practices remain unchanged: 128 gridworld seeds, five main Atari seeds, 120 LunarLander seeds, and three RMSprop seeds per game. Confidence intervals, stratified bootstrap intervals, and standard-deviation reporting are retained.

E6.justification: Figure 2 changes numerically: the 500-timestep episode-completion improvement at k=0.4 falls from approximately 17% to 9% under the same stated protocol. Figure 6 also changes under the revised 57-game aggregation, so it is not a same-setting performance comparison. Figures 3–5 and 7–8 and Table 2 retain their results.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 repairs Proposition 3's summation to S_q=(1+k)S_z. Appendix B corrects the chain rule to differentiate through the chosen action's Q-value, and Proposition 5 restores the absolute value around the residual mean. These repair existing reasoning without adding new theoretical results.

C1.justification: The central claims remain parameter-free value sharing through lower-norm residuals, faster learning and improved aggregate Atari performance, reduced overestimation, and increased action gaps. Abstract and conclusion edits preserve their scientific scope.

C2.justification: Section 7 adds an interpretation of the layer as generalization across actions, acknowledges that ordinary DQN already generalizes through shared parameters, and identifies possible approximation errors as a tradeoff requiring investigation. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds JAX code alongside the unchanged PyTorch implementation. Appendix E.2 removes the explicit statement that IQN's exploration-decay schedule matches DQN, making that detail less explicit. The repository access information and numerical hyperparameter table remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bradbury et al. (2018) for JAX. Positioning relative to Dueling DQN, RDQ, advantage-based methods, and normalization remains substantively unchanged; other bibliography edits concern existing references.

P1.justification: Local copyediting improves grammar, terminology, mathematical exposition, and several discussion paragraphs. Appendix D's heading expands to include JAX. The overall narrative and section/appendix sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with a revised vertical scale and a legend moved from lower right to upper left. Figure 6's caption changes its game count. The added JAX listing causes local appendix reflow, and Table 1 newly marks the step size as differing from original DQN.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical correctness through the Proposition 3 and tabular-gradient repairs, adds a JAX implementation, and explicitly discusses approximation-error tradeoffs. These are useful refinements to otherwise stable contributions and main results. The less explicit IQN exploration schedule and undocumented reason for the gridworld curve revisions limit the gain.
